newEntriesNeeded.title: Dynamic Menu Creation in PML Forms
newEntriesNeeded.principle: PML forms support dynamic menu creation via !this.newMenu() and bar.add() methods, enabling runtime popup and bar menus.
newEntriesNeeded.rule: Use !this.newMenu('menuName') to create a menu object, then .add('callback', 'label', 'command') to add entries. Use !this.bar.add('category', 'name') for bar menu entries.
newEntriesNeeded.exampleAntipattern:
-- Static menu defined at form setup (less flexible)
!menu = menu
!menu.add('Static', '.staticMethod')
pitfalls: Menu names must be unique within the form scope
Callback commands are strings, not method references
Bar menu categories appear as submenus
newEntriesNeeded.sourcedoc: AVEVA PML Customization Guide - Forms and Menus

newEntriesNeeded.title: DO VALUES Iteration over ARRAY Elements
newEntriesNeeded.principle: PML supports iterating over ARRAY elements using DO ... VALUES ... ENDDO, which yields each populated element as the loop index.
newEntriesNeeded.rule: Use DO !index VALUES !arrayName to iterate over all populated elements. !index holds the value of each element (not the position).
newEntriesNeeded.syntax:
DO !index VALUES !arrayName
  -- !index contains each element value
ENDDO
newEntriesNeeded.exampleCanonical:
-- Iterate over selected list items
!selectedItems = !this.list.val
do !index values !selectedItems
  !viewName = !this.list.rtext[!index]
  !this.processView(!viewName)
enddo
newEntriesNeeded.exampleAntipattern:
-- Using FROM/TO with array Size() when VALUES is more natural
!i = 1
do while !i.le(!selectedItems.Size())
  !index = !selectedItems[!i]
  !i = !i + 1
enddo
pitfalls: !index holds the element value, not the array index
Use !selectedItems[!index] to access array by value when values are indices
Array indices in PML start at 1
newEntriesNeeded.sourcedoc: AVEVA PML Customization Guide - Control Logic

newEntriesNeeded.title: defined() Check for Global Form Objects
newEntriesNeeded.principle: Use defined() to check if a global form object exists before attempting to access it, preventing runtime errors.
newEntriesNeeded.rule: Use if(defined(!!globalForm)) to check existence. If the form exists, access its methods; otherwise, create a new instance.
newEntriesNeeded.syntax:
if(defined(!!globalForm)) then
  !!globalForm.method()
else
  !!globalVar = object CLASS()
endif
newEntriesNeeded.exampleCanonical:
-- Safe access to global logger form
if(defined(!!ramcommonloggerform)) then
  !!ramcommonloggerform.clearData()
else
  !!RAMCOMMONLOGGER = object RAMCOMMONLOGGER()
endif
newEntriesNeeded.exampleAntipattern:
-- Direct access without check (will error if form not loaded)
!!ramcommonloggerform.clearData()
pitfalls: defined() checks variable existence, not object validity
Global form names are case-insensitive in PML

newEntriesNeeded.title: FILE Object set() and exists() Pattern
newEntriesNeeded.principle: The FILE object requires .set() to resolve the path before .exists() can reliably check for the file or folder.
newEntriesNeeded.rule: Create FILE object with path, call .set() to resolve, then use .exists() to check. Combine with AND for conditional logic.
newEntriesNeeded.syntax:
!file = object FILE(!path)
if(!file.set() AND !file.exists()) then
  -- file/folder exists
else
  -- handle missing
endif
newEntriesNeeded.exampleCanonical:
!file = object FILE(!outputFolder.val)
if(!file.set() AND !file.exists()) then
  -- proceed with export
else
  !!alert.warning('Please select valid output folder')
endif
newEntriesNeeded.exampleAntipattern:
-- Checking exists without set (may fail on relative paths)
!file = object FILE(!path)
if(!file.exists()) then
pitfalls: .set() resolves the path and returns success/failure
.exists() checks both files and folders
Use .fullname() to get resolved absolute path

newEntriesNeeded.title: NETGRIDCONTROL with NETDATASOURCE Binding
newEntriesNeeded.principle: NETGRIDCONTROL from GridControl add-in can be bound to data via NETDATASOURCE object for dynamic data display.
newEntriesNeeded.rule: Create NETGRIDCONTROL object, configure properties (columnExcelFilter, fixedRows, etc.), create NETDATASOURCE with columns and rows, then bind with bindToDataSource().
newEntriesNeeded.syntax:
using namespace 'Aveva.Core.Presentation'
!grid = object NETGRIDCONTROL()
!grid.columnExcelFilter(true)
!grid.fixedRows(true)
!nds = object NETDATASOURCE('name', !headings, !rows)
!grid.bindToDataSource(!nds)
newEntriesNeeded.exampleAntipattern:
-- Direct assignment without binding (no data display)
!grid = object NETGRIDCONTROL()
!grid.data = !rows
pitfalls: NETGRIDCONTROL requires GridControl import
NETDATASOURCE namespace must be set
Column names in headings must match data array dimensions

newEntriesNeeded.title: Container Gadget with PMLNETCONTROL Type
newEntriesNeeded.principle: PML container gadgets can host .NET controls via PMLNETCONTROL sub-type, enabling rich data grids and custom UI elements.
newEntriesNeeded.rule: Declare container gadget with PMLNETCONTROL and a sub-type string. Set the .control property to the .NET object's handle().
newEntriesNeeded.syntax:
container .contName PMLNETCONTROL 'SUBTYPE' anchor all at x y wid h
-- In method:
!this.contName.control = !netObject.handle()
newEntriesNeeded.exampleCanonical:
container .coSelectionList PMLNETCONTROL 'NET' anchor all at xmax+2 ymin width 80 height 20
-- In constructor:
!this.coSelectionList.control = !this.gridSelectionList.handle()
newEntriesNeeded.exampleAntipattern:
-- Using container without PMLNETCONTROL for .NET controls
container .coSelectionList anchor all at xmax+2 ymin width 80 height 20
pitfalls: PMLNETCONTROL requires GridControl or appropriate import
The .control property must be set to the .NET object's handle()
Container must be anchored for proper resizing

newEntriesNeeded.title: PMLFolderBrowser Object for Folder Selection
newEntriesNeeded.principle: PMLFolderBrowser provides a standard folder selection dialog accessible from PML forms.
newEntriesNeeded.rule: Create PMLFolderBrowser object, call .show(title, mode) to display, then read .selectedPath() for the result.
newEntriesNeeded.syntax:
using namespace 'Aveva.Core.Presentation'
!browser = object PMLFOLDERBROWSER()
!browser.show('Select Folder', true)
!path = !browser.selectedPath()
newEntriesNeeded.exampleCanonical:
using namespace 'Aveva.Core.Presentation'
!folderBrowser = object PMLFOLDERBROWSER()
!folderBrowser.show('Select Output Folder', true)
!this.teOutputFolder.val = !folderBrowser.selectedPath()
newEntriesNeeded.exampleAntipattern:
-- Using FILE object for folder browsing (less user-friendly)
!file = object FILE('')
!file.browse()
pitfalls: PMLFOLDERBROWSER requires Aveva.Core.Presentation namespace
selectedPath() returns empty string if dialog cancelled
Second parameter of .show() controls multi-select mode

newEntriesNeeded.title: !!alert.warning() System Alert Method
newEntriesNeeded.principle: The !!alert global object provides a .warning() method for displaying warning messages to users.
newEntriesNeeded.rule: Use !!alert.warning('message') to display a non-fatal warning dialog.
newEntriesNeeded.exampleCanonical:
if(!isDetailsSet) then
  !!alert.warning('PML Function cannot be previewed')
else
  -- process data
endif
newEntriesNeeded.exampleAntipattern:
-- Using $P for user-facing messages (goes to command line, not visible)
$P Warning: no data selected
pitfalls: !!alert.warning() is non-blocking
Message text should be concise and actionable
Use for user-facing warnings, not debug output
